content.thinking:
I need to plan the file structure carefully before writing it all at once without testing incrementally. I'm thinking through whether the builder requires a root joint, and deciding to create a safe root joint at the origin that other parts can attach to by default.

Now I'm sketching out the chest's real-world proportions — roughly 0.8m wide, 0.5m deep body, 0.4m tall, with the lid tilted open — and positioning it centered along x with the front facing +Z. I'm planning helper functions for boxes and parts, using toon-style cel paints for the wood, gold, navy, and velvet surfaces while staying under part and color limits by merging coin geometries per color group, and considering how to add coin face detail without blowing up the part count.

Still writing coin generation logic...

For stacked coins I'll add slight jitter to each position for a natural look. Then for gems, I'll use flat-shaded octahedron and dodecahedron geometries colored by gem type—ruby, sapphire, emerald, amethyst.

I'm deciding against fully glowing the gems since that would wash out faceted shading; instead I'll apply a moderate glow (around 0.45 intensity) across all gems so the emissive color still lets facets read clearly, wrapping each part in the glow helper individually.

Now I'm shaping the gem geometry, building a brilliant-cut profile with a lathe outline for the top and bottom facets...

For the chest body itself, I'm thinking I'll construct it as a box with navy cel-shaded paint, then build open wooden walls so the interior reads correctly beneath the coin pile.

I'm simplifying to a solid navy box for the chest, then adding gold trim framing the rim, corner brackets, horizontal bands, and a lock plate featuring a lion face, which I could render as an SVG texture mapped onto a plane rather than building it from geometry.

Now I'm adding fleur-de-lis decals on the front panel and a torus ring handle on the side, then working out how to build the hinged, tilted-open lid as a separate group with navy outer and red inner plates plus gold frame rails, defined in local lid coordinates before transforming into place.

Computing the hinge rotation angle (around -105°) so the lid's local axes map correctly into world space, confirming the outer face ends up pointing backward as intended.

Working out the lid's layered construction: a navy outer slab with a thin red lining inside facing the viewer, plus gold frame rails along both the outer and inner edges to add visible trim.

I'll compute the hinge pivot and lid rotation using a transform matrix, placing it at (0, 0.40, -0.22) where the body's top edge sits, then checking that the lid's extended geometry and the crown's height both fit comfortably within the overall proportions without clipping.

For the coin pile on top, I'm generating roughly 160 randomly positioned and tilted cylindrical coins across the chest's surface using a mound-shaped height function, then reducing segment count to around 10 per coin to keep the triangle budget near 50k instead of blowing past 60k.

Now I'm planning a scattered ring of loose coins around the chest's base—about 120 pieces placed within an elliptical region outside the chest's footprint, with heights varying to suggest small piles spilling onto the floor.

I'll add denser mounds beneath the scattered coins (around 260 total) so nothing appears to float, plus four small stacks of 6-10 coins near the front corners, bringing the coin count to roughly 465 pieces and 23k triangles total—still reasonable. Next I'm setting up two goblets, with one standing upright on the chest's top right area.

Working out the viewer's left/right orientation relative to the model's +X axis, I'm placing the upright goblet on the image-left side near the crown, and the tipped-over goblet on the image-right with its base hanging past the chest edge. I'll build the goblet shape using a lathe profile with a foot, stem, knop, and open bowl.

Writing lathe profile coordinates...

Checking that the inner and outer edges don't cross confirms the geometry is fine, so I won't smooth these segments. Now I'm figuring out placement for gem studs around the goblet's bowl, computing the radius at a given height to position ruby decorations correctly around the axis.

For the rim, I'll add a thin torus ring, then for the tipped goblet I need a reusable transform helper that applies rotation and origin offset to local points so the same builder function works for both upright and tilted versions. I'm also sketching out the crown's base band using a lathe profile with a stepped outer cylinder shape.

Now I'm designing the crown's fleur points and crossing arches -- spikes with gem tips at the band, plus two arcing bands sweeping via catmull curves across the top from front to back, forming the classic crossed-arch crown silhouette.

Topping it with a small cross and a red velvet dome (a scaled half-sphere), I'm adding an ermine band of white cylinder painted with black spots, a large ruby oval centered at front with a gold bezel torus, and a ring of small sapphires around the base. I'm positioning the whole crown tilted slightly and resting into the coin pile, then threading a hanging strand of pearls down the chest using spheres placed along a catmull path.

Now I'm laying out a second gold-bead necklace with a V-shaped catmull path beside the lion pendant, placing around 22 small gold spheres along it.

Then I'm adding a sapphire pendant at the bottom with a gold bezel, checking spacing so the pearls and lion plate don't overlap, and positioning gold corner bars and rim frame bands along the top edges of the piece.

Now I'm laying out the base band, vertical corner posts with pyramid-shaped shoulder caps, fleur-de-lis decal planes on the front panel, and rows of merged gold rivet studs along the bands.

I'm designing a diamond-shaped shield plate extruded with bevel, overlaid with a lion texture plane and a hanging gold ring below the mouth, plus a torus-shaped handle ring on the side.

For the lid, I'm planning navy outer face with gold frame bands and a corner diamond ornament topped with sapphire, while the inner side gets red velvet-style shading with tiny stud tufts.

Now I'm working out the lid's geometry: adding gold edge bands along the thin side walls, and figuring out local dimensions (width, hinge position, front edge) so the lid aligns correctly with the body and hinge location in world space.

For the outer slab, I'm defining its box dimensions and position, using a mottled navy paint wrapped in a cel-shading function, then checking that the lighting logic correctly reads world-space normals so the back-facing lid surface falls into shadow under the key light.

Continuing the geometry, I'm placing the inner red lining box just inside the lid surface and verifying it overlaps correctly without clipping through, then starting on the gold inside frame rails as four boxes.

Adding a central diamond ornament using a four-sided cylinder rotated to form a diamond shape, with a sapphire-like octahedron sphere on top, and working out the local quaternion rotation needed to orient it along the outward normal.

Defining lid placement helpers and fixed-box builders, then thinking through a more painterly gold color using mottled texture with a derived cel shadow.

For geometry, I'm planning to merge coins, chest body, and bands into single parts using BufferGeometryUtils to reduce draw calls, as long as all attribute types line up across primitives.

Coins get split into two groups with slightly different gold tones for variety, plus a merged circular face mesh textured with a fleur pattern facing up, tilted randomly so some lean without needing a bottom face.

Designing the coin face SVG with a golden circle, ring outline, and a simple fleur-de-lis made from an ellipse, mirrored curves, and a small band shape.

For the lion SVG, I'm generating a mane as a spiky star polygon in gold tones, with a lighter circular face, small ears, dark eyes and nose, and muzzle lines, sizing the stroke widths appropriately for the viewBox scale.

Now I'm working out gem placements for the treasure pile, assigning positions, colors, sizes, and rotations for rubies, emeralds, amethysts, and sapphires scattered both on the floor and atop the coin mound, adjusting their heights to match the pile's contours near the chest.

Working out coin placement near the chest, using distance-based rejection sampling to scatter them naturally with slight random tilts, then handling the coins piled on top with a similar falloff formula for height based on distance from center.

Now I'm positioning the crown and goblet on the pile, calculating their resting heights against the curved pile surface, checking that the goblet doesn't collide with the lid geometry, and starting to set up a second goblet lying tipped on its side.

Checking the stem placement: the foot sits where it crosses the chest rim at x=0.41, y=0.40, giving a stem length that works out nicely resting on the edge. I'll place foot y at 0.38 and scatter a few gold coins spilling from the goblet's mouth for added detail.

Now I'm working out the chest body texture—painting it as navy wooden planks with darker seams between rows, alternating shades between plank rows to give a subtle banded look, layered under the cel shading pass.

Setting up the gold paint using a mottled yellow-gold cel shader with darker shadow tones for the hardware, keeping small pieces flat-colored while bands and trim get the richer paint. Now I'm defining the lion plate as a shield-shaped extrusion with a sharp bottom point and smoothed edges.

Working out the extrusion axis and positioning for the chest plate, lock plate, lion decal, and the small ring detail, placing each at specific coordinates along the chest's front face so they sit flush with the surface without rotation needed since the torus already faces the right direction.

I'm also setting up the pearl and bead decoration along a catmull-rom path using b.along to place spheres at sampled points, and double-checking my imports so I don't trip the typechecker with unused ones.

Now I'm working out the crown geometry in local coordinates with a placer function for the origin and quaternion, figuring out how the lathe operation should handle the axis parameter for the band piece.

Defining crown geometry coordinates...

Computing arch curve points so they rise high enough to clear the velvet dome at each radius, checking apex and mid-span heights against the dome surface.

Now I'm placing the two crossed golden arches as swept tube paths, adding a top orb with a cross ornament, and positioning gem shapes like the front ruby as a flattened oval sphere on the band's front face.

I'm defining the bezel torus for the crown band, scattering small studded sapphire spheres around it at angular offsets, and setting the crown's origin position and tilt orientation using an Euler rotation.

Now I'm writing a lathe-based gem geometry helper that defines the profile points for a faceted gem with a flat table top, and considering the vertex winding/normal direction risk that could make the gem render as hollow if the lathe orientation is wrong.

For variety, I'm planning gem shape variations—using fewer segments for emerald-cut square pyramids versus more for rounded gems—and designing a floor gem placement list with position, color, radius, height, segment count, and tilt so gems can sit upright or lying with slight rotation, sunk slightly into the floor surface.

I'm also planning sparkle effects: small star-shaped billboard planes positioned near gem tops, angled toward the camera with alpha-cut textures to create a glinting glow, roughly eight per big gem using emissive map textures for the shine.

There's no ground plane since the chest is a standalone prop, so I need coins resting flush at y=0 without sinking below it—accounting for tilt angle so the lowest edge of each tilted coin still sits at the floor height plus a small offset based on its radius and thickness.

Now I'm defining the coin stacks: setting spacing between stacked coins slightly larger than their thickness, adding small random jitter in position and yaw, and placing several stack groups around the chest at specific x,z coordinates with varying heights (5-9 coins each) to create a natural scattered pile effect.

I'm adding small chest details: rim torus on coins (skipping for simplicity), hidden rear hinges, corner posts, and a row of brass rivets along the front plank band made from merged small spheres. I'm also considering gold corner caps at the top of the chest using small cone shapes.

Now I'm working out overall dimensions — lid height, coin spill width, and floor extents — to make sure the chest with its coin pile reads as roughly 0.8-0.9m tall and nearly 2m wide including spilled coins.

Setting up a rejection sampling scheme for scattering coins on the floor: coins inside the chest's footprint get rejected, while those outside fall off in a soft elliptical falloff so the pile thins naturally toward the edges.

Now I'm writing a helper that builds each coin by composing a transform matrix from position and rotation, then applying it to cylinder geometry for the coin body and circle geometry for its face, splitting coins randomly between two batches for rendering variety.

Still wiring up the merged geometry...

Checking the color budget stays under 64 total across gold tones, gems, pearl, and accents, and confirming the chest, coins, and other pieces all sit properly at ground level with no floating parts.

Now I'm setting up the file imports and scaffolding for the model builder, pulling in the geometry utilities, paint helpers, path and math utilities, and the toon/glow kits needed before defining the meta object.

Writing module imports and setup...

Now I'm defining the gold and navy color palettes for this treasure hoard, using mottled and celled paint effects to give the gold a weathered, hand-painted look, and setting up wood grain textures for the planks.

Writing box-part helper function...

Adding gold trim rim and posts...

I'm placing rivet rows as small spheres along the body edges, skipping the lion plate area, plus bottom band rivets and corner caps for detail.

Now I'm adding corner cone accents rotated 45 degrees to align with the square shape, plus fleur-de-lis decal planes on the front and side panels for decoration.

I'm also placing hanging ring handles made from small torus shapes mounted on boss plates on each side, mirrored for both the left and right faces.

For the lid, I'm attaching diamond studs at the corners, positioning it via a hinge point at the back edge, and adding gold outer and inner rail trim plus small cone-shaped corner caps on the outer face.

Still writing cone rotation...

Then I'm adding gold cross-bands across the outside of the lid with a central diamond ornament, and for the inside I'm setting up a red lining with a 3x4 grid of small gold button tufts.

I'll unify all the geometry collection into a single merge-by-color-key helper so parts with the same material get batched together, then add a diamond quilting pattern to the lining via a paint-based texture.

Now I'm placing a sapphire octahedron ornament on the lid, then working out the pile of coins and gems on top using a height function that bulges toward the center and tapers near the edges, positioning the crown and scattering several colored gems (sapphire, ruby, emerald) across the mound.

I'm also building the goblets as lathed shapes oriented along a custom axis from an origin point, with decorative studs like a ring of ruby beads placed around the knop using local cylindrical coordinates.

I'm now adding the rim and band torus shapes around the bowl, orienting them so their ring axis lines up with the goblet's own vertical direction, and sizing their radii to fit snugly between the bowl's existing curves.

For the tipped-over goblet, I'm scattering a few extra coins near its mouth to suggest spilled treasure, letting them blend into the main coin pile rather than tracking them separately. I'm also sketching out a sparkle effect using a simple four-pointed star SVG path, filled white with a warm glow for a magical highlight.

Now I'm sizing up the scene's overall part budget—boxes, gems, sparkles, crown pieces, and goblets—keeping the total well under 300 parts, and checking triangle counts for the lathed gems and low-poly pearl spheres to make sure everything stays lightweight. I'm also setting up a reusable sphere helper function for the pearls.

I'm defining a gem geometry generator using LatheGeometry to create faceted gem shapes, with an addGem helper that applies glow and positions them with tilted rotations so they appear to lie naturally within the pile rather than standing upright.

Working out positioning for scattered floor gems...

Still calculating stack positions and floor heights...

Now I'm planning the bag-flush logic grouping geometry by key with color and texture, then building the spiky lion emblem shape with alternating outer and inner radius points around the circle.

Writing SVG code...

Finishing the fleur-de-lis petals and band, then starting a layered gold coin SVG with concentric circles in different shades.

Still resolving color types...

Now I'm placing the quilted lining slab and gold inner rail positions, checking that the lining sits slightly proud of the lid surface by 0.01, and aligning the front/back/side rails so they frame the lid slab edges correctly.

Working out the outer rails and cross bands next, positioning them around the diamond centerpiece so the bands sit above and below it without overlapping, then adding a hidden vertical center band beneath the diamond and starting the diamond shape itself as a small four-sided cylinder.

For the diamond gem I'm layering a dark inner cylinder inside the outer gold one, then adding a sapphire octahedron on top for the glow effect, considering whether to scale it flatter using an octahedron geometry and working through how orientation (quaternion vs rotation) should be prioritized for the gem placement function.

Writing lid detail geometry...

Only spheres and cylinders go into the merge bag, keeping gold rivets grouped by color. I'm separating the coins and faces into their own maps, creating the face texture part with its position and bone binding, then writing the addCoin helper and assembling the final crown code while skipping extra floor decorations.

Setting up the crown's rotation, placement, and axis orientation, then writing a helper function `cpart` that places geometry pieces with consistent quaternion and optional scale. I'm also sketching out the lathe shapes for the crown band and preparing an angular loop to position points around it.

Now I'm adding gold spikes around the crown points, alternating tall and short lengths with gemstone tips in ruby and sapphire, plus a glow effect on the taller ones. Then I'm setting up the ermine lathe with spotted fur coloring, and starting on a velvet sphere cap geometry for the crown's interior.

Writing crown jewel placement code...

Adding the orb top with a small sphere, cross piece, and gem for the pendant.

Now I'm positioning the bezel with a torus ring and elliptical sapphire sphere, then routing chain points to drape over the rim's front edge from top to bottom. I'm also laying out a pearl strand with fourteen beads following a similar draping path down the front.

For the goblets, I'm computing orientation quaternions so one goblet tips toward a direction vector while another stays upright, then writing a helper function that places each goblet and derives its lathe axis from the quaternion before generating the lathe geometry with gold coloring.

Adding torus rims and studded details...

I need to add a floor slab beneath the body, checking that the top face aligns without z-fighting, then define a mound height function that clamps to a minimum inside a bounded range. I'm also setting up a randomized coin-scattering loop on top, placing coins at random x/z positions offset above the mound surface.

Estimating total triangle counts across coins, pearls, gems, lathed goblets, tori, and boxes to stay under the budget, I land around 38k which should be fine. Now I'm writing the tilt randomization function for placement offsets.

I'm defining a type for gem data with position, color, radius, height, segment count, and rotation, then adding a few gems scattered on top of the pile. Time to write the actual file now along with the meta description and style.
